architecture: v3 (Pellbrook Metro's 2027 headway management programme: which four of the eight frequent bus routes get the operator's supervisor teams, ranked on the excess wait per weekday-peak boarding on each route's frequent corridor in the August census fortnight, each rider's wait measured against the buses that serve the stop they tag off at)
slot_note: re-drawn at architecture 3, the number's last, in a new domain: the bus world of seed DA20 (the headway programme, eight frequent routes, four branching beyond a shared corridor), its frequent-network population step a WHAT and so not taken; task270 draws its own world
niche: a frequent bus network whose four branched routes send alternate buses to two branches beyond a shared corridor, so a corridor rider bound for a corridor stop can take either branch's bus and one bound for a branch only that branch's
answer: Give the 2027 headway supervisor teams to routes 3, 7, 31 and 40.
answer_source: task269/submission.md, block 1 (Final Recommendation); retired 2026-10-19, not shipped
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every file and rule correctly works each route's excess wait at its corridor timing points from all of the route's departures (the standard's average wait under random arrival, less the timetable's), weights it by the route's corridor boardings and gives the teams to routes 3, 7, 14 and 31; on the four branched routes alternate buses serve different branches, so a rider bound for a branch can take only that branch's buses, and measuring each rider's wait against the buses that serve the stop they tag off at drops route 14 and puts 40 in.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the expected excess wait of passengers arriving at random at a stop on a shared corridor, worked over the attractive set of lines serving each rider's destination (the common-lines problem of transit network analysis), riders bound for the corridor facing both branches' combined headways and riders bound for a branch only that branch's; with another field's nouns (patients for riders, wards for routes) there are no headways, random arrivals or branches sharing a trunk, so the task stops reading the same.
layer1: the location vendor's timing-point departures as first released and as revised after its unmatched pings were re-run, both covering the fortnight
near-duplicate departure records where a bus reopened its doors at a timing point
tag-on and tag-off journeys with a few per cent of tag-offs missing (default fares)
two timetable feeds, the second in force from Monday 17 August with new running times on every frequent route
stops renumbered at a relocation during the fortnight, recorded in the stop changes log
stakeholder_role: Pellbrook Metro's network performance manager (Pellbrook City Council's public transport business), who runs the headway management programme and puts its 2027 routes to the council's Public Transport Committee

spine.entity: one bus's departure from one timing point on one trip on one service day
spine.grain: trip x timing point x service day
spine.row_meaning: the location vendor's revised record of a bus leaving a timing point
spine.source_dataset: constructed (seeded generator; the city, its transport agency, the bus operator and people are fictional)

world.geography: Australia (the city of Pellbrook, its council's public transport business, the bus operator and people are fictional)
world.org_type: city council's public transport business (the frequent routes run under contract)

driver: The decisive quantity is the expected excess wait of units arriving at random at a point served by interleaved streams of departures, where units bound for some destinations can take any stream and units bound for others only one, so each unit's wait is worked over the departures serving its own destination, read from a second file at the unit's grain; the measure over all departures overstates the units tied to one stream wherever the streams bunch with each other, and the measure over the stream each unit happened to take understates the units that could take any.
driver_concrete: Each corridor rider's excess wait at the timing point is worked from the headways of the buses serving the stop they tag off at, riders bound for corridor stops (and every inbound rider) over both branches' combined departures and riders bound for a branch over that branch's alone, so routes whose branches run as bunched pairs while each branch keeps its own interval fall back and the four routes are 3, 7, 31 and 40, not the route-level measure's 3, 7, 14 and 31.
stump: A competent solver works each route's excess wait from all of its departures at the corridor timing points, weights it by corridor boardings and gives the teams to routes 3, 7, 14 and 31 (or, splitting by the branch of the bus each rider boarded, drops route 7 for route 9); the step that lands it there is taking the route, or the boarded bus, as each rider's service when a rider bound for a branch can take only that branch's buses and one bound for the corridor either.

differentiation.task263: task263 recovers each source's own level from samples that blend the sources by a mass balance; nothing here is blended or recovered: each rider's expected wait is worked over the departures serving that rider's destination, a usable set read from the rider's tag-off, and the error corrected is waiting counted against buses the rider could not take.
differentiation.task120: task120 v1 forms a unit no file stores through a two-hop join before cutting percentiles; here the unit, the rider's journey, sits on every row, and the decisive move is which departures make up that rider's wait, not which records group.
differentiation.task239: task239 nets member-level covariance out of group means in a factor analysis; nothing here is a covariance: the expected wait under random arrival is worked over a destination-dependent subset of interleaved departure streams.
differentiation.task264: task264 v1 moves the unit up to the chain that sets a price so volume shifts between setters do not pass for price change; here the move goes below the route to the departures each rider can take, set by where that rider is going.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how consistently a total over several scored parts will rank units once each part is scored by one scorer drawn from a pool and different units meet different scorers, estimated from a round in which the same two scorers scored every unit on each part; in that round a scorer's own level was shared by every unit and so never moved a ranking, so the agreement between parts, each scorer's marks taken alone and a decomposition that keeps the scorers shared all leave it out, while under the new arrangement it adds to every unit's error, so the number of parts has to come from the round's sources of variance recombined with the scorers' levels counted as error.
lineage.architecture: v1 (Callowfield University's 2027 final-year OSCE, single-examined in three parallel circuits once Fennabeg Clinical School's cohort joins: the number of stations its total marks need for the school's reliability standard of 0.80, projected from the 2026 sitting's dual-examined marks with each station's examiner stringency counted as error)
lineage.stump: A competent solver computes the 2026 sitting's reliability on single-examiner marks (alpha across the stations, or a generalizability study with the examiners crossed with the candidates) and steps it to more stations by Spearman-Brown, filing the current 12 stations as enough; the step that lands it there is reading each examiner's leniency as 2026 showed it, a shift every candidate at that station shared, when in 2027's parallel circuits different candidates meet different examiners and the leniency spread between examiners becomes error in every candidate's total.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-19 at stage 4 (Gate F): the cold reader split the 2026 marks into candidates by examiners within stations and counted the stringency as error for one examiner a station, committing the golden call and every ask figure; the judge DETERMINISTIC with Gates G and H passing

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how consistently a total over parts will rank units when the specification fixes how many parts come from each content area every time, so each unit's strength in an area recurs in every form and belongs to the true score; estimated from a round whose parts were drawn the same way, the analysis that treats the parts as drawn from one undivided pool counts that strength as error and overstates the number of parts a standard needs.
lineage.architecture: v2 (Callowfield University's 2027 final OSCE, single-examined in three parallel circuits on a blueprint that draws the same number of stations from each of four domains every year: the number of stations for the school's 0.80 reliability standard, from the 2026 marks' variance components with each candidate's domain-specific strength counted as true score under the fixed blueprint and the examiner's stringency as error)
lineage.stump: A competent solver fits the 2026 marks' variance components with the stations and examiners random from one bank, counts the examiner's stringency as error for one examiner a station and files 16 stations; the step that lands it there is counting the candidate-by-domain variance as error, when the blueprint draws the same number of stations from each domain every year, so a candidate's domain strengths recur in every form and belong to what the total mark measures.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-19 at stage 4 round 3 (Gate F): of six scored readers five filed 16 stations by the pooled decision study and the sixth stratified the 2026 marks by the blueprint's domains under policy 4.2 and landed the call (13) and every reliability; the judge's pass 3 found Ask B's namesake device unfair, repaired before round 3
